newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentinian praises Tunisia for moderation.
newsitem.headline: Argentinian praises Tunisia for moderation.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali, on a three-day visit to Argentina, met President Carlos Menem Tuesday and went to Congress where he heard praise for Tunisia's role in turbulent North Africa.

At a reception for him in the Senate in Buenos Aires, Vice-President Carlos Ruckauf hailed Tunisia's "vocation for moderation in a rebellious region" as well as its "economic growth and drive for liberalisation."

Earlier, Menem thanked Ben Ali for his country's "unconditional" support in Argentina's territorial dispute with Britain over the Falklands, and told him: "Your country may seem distant in geography but it is close to our hearts."

Senior officials from both countries were due to sign a bilateral accord on Tuesday on cooperation on the environment, animal health, agriculture and on general economic, cultural and educational cooperation.

But the real impetus behind the visit, to end Wednesday, is trade in energy, agriculture, tourism and shipping. The Argentine oil company Pluspetrol has been exploring for oil on the border between Tunisia and Libya since 1994.
Two-way trade between Tunisia and Argentina grew to $108 million in 1996 from $28 million a year earlier.

Menem has visited Tunisia twice but it is the first visit to Argentina for Ben Ali, who told the Senate of his appreciation for the "seriousness and sincerity" of bilateral relations and "the mutual political will to strengthen the links of friendship between Argentina and Tunisia."
